title: Longest Common Subsequence
summary: Find the length of the longest sequence of letters that appears, in order, in both strings.

tests.explain: "one" appears in both, in order: st-o-n-e and l-o-n-g-e-st. No common subsequence of length 4 exists.
A string is a subsequence of itself.
No letter appears in both strings.

hints: Compare the last letters of the two strings. If they are equal, can they both be part of the answer?
Let dp[i][j] be the answer for the first i letters of text1 and the first j letters of text2. Add an extra row and column of zeros for the empty prefixes.
If text1[i - 1] === text2[j - 1], dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1. Otherwise dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]). The answer is dp[m][n].

complexity.time: O(m × n): one constant-time cell per pair of prefixes
complexity.space: O(m × n) for the table (O(min(m, n)) with two rows)
